muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free.decidedBy: owner review 2026-08-20, on the OpenCode Zen contributor disclosure
evidence: OpenCode documents the exact free contributor offer as muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free and identifies it as the Muse Spark 1.2 contributor variant.

The reference index publishes meta/muse-spark-1.2 as the base model identity, and Muse Spark is listed under meta/ by several independent resellers, so the vendor attribution is not inferred from OpenCode alone.

The index ALSO publishes meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor as a separate entry. Compared field by field it is the same model: identical release date, 1,048,576 context, 131,072 output, attachment and reasoning. Only the price differs — $1.25/$4.25 against $0.10/$0.20 — so the contributor entry records different commercial terms, not different capabilities. Quality belongs to the model and is attributed to the base identity; the contributor terms stay on the offer, where cost is already scored per provider/model.
Contributor evaluation is explicitly owner-approved and remains recorded separately as a consented evaluation identity.
muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free.yields: measured VQ from the exact meta/muse-spark-1.2 benchmark entry; local contributor runtime evidence remains on the provider offer
muse-spark-1.2-contributor-free.reverifyBy: if OpenCode changes the contributor offer disclosure, or if meta/muse-spark-1.2-contributor stops matching the base model on capabilities and limits rather than only on price

rejected.note: Identity candidates that were examined and REFUSED on evidence, plus the cases where the search established that no candidate exists at all. These are records of a DECISION, never a resolution: nothing here may ever become a resolved identity. They are ingested into the catalog so the dashboard can answer 'what did we actually do to reach identity_review' rather than leaving the work in a file no consumer reads. Each candidate is kept as its own record — two rejected candidates are two facts, not one paragraph.
